words.prose: {{ar:دُونِهِمَا}} ({{tr:dūnihimā}}) is the ayah's relational engine. Governed by {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}), it functions as the core of the fronted predicate, so the clause first says where or how the new pair stands before it says what the pair is. The suffix {{ar:هِمَا}} ({{tr:himā}}) makes the comparison point definite: the phrase reaches back to the earlier two gardens at 55:46, across the intervening description and refrain, even though the following noun will reveal another dual pair. Its local range should stay broad enough to carry below, lesser, and besides/other-than together; that blend makes the garden relation spatial, hierarchical, and distinct without collapsing the two pairs into one. The same word is not about registering or cataloguing, and a same-ayah cataphoric possibility is secondary to the stronger backward garden reference. Its nasal chain with {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}) and the suffix makes the preposition, relational noun, and pronoun sound like one compact predicate frame. After the challenge at 55:61, that frame turns the response into spatially ordered bounty. In the surah's larger usage, a common exclusion formula is re-specialized here into ordered bounty: the other-than pressure that can mark contested loyalty in 18:50 and 34:41 becomes the ranking of paradisal gardens.

words.prose: {{ar:جَنَّتَانِ}} ({{tr:jannatāni}}) is the delayed subject that resolves the fronted rank phrase. Its ending fuses dual number with nominative subjecthood, so the final word both names exactly two fresh gardens and prevents the noun from being swallowed as a genitive complement of {{ar:دُونِهِمَا}} ({{tr:dūnihimā}}). Because the noun is indefinite, it introduces a new pair, while its exact dual recurrence from 55:46 makes the new pair a matched second panel rather than a generic paradise field. The j-n-n root selects the covered garden branch here: the gardens are imagined as enclosed, shaded, and hidden reward-spaces, with protective-cover and inner-hiddenness associations adding texture while madness, hidden-being, and other branches are blocked as local senses. That sense split also matters in Surah 55's address world: hidden addressees and hidden reward-space share the root field, but this word names the reward, not the beings. With {{ar:دُونِهِمَا}} ({{tr:dūnihimā}}), the d-w-n and j-n-n root pair that can appear in contested loyalty settings at 18:50 and 34:41 is narrowed here into garden hierarchy. The word closes the ayah on the disclosed bounty after 55:61, and its pair remains open for later specification by the dual adjective at 55:64. It also stands bare of the usual river pairing, so the garden formula is invoked while this panel waits for its own descriptors.

summary.what_was_special: The focus verse is unusually productive because its two roots cross spatial rank, alterity, proximity, botanical enclosure, protection, dense growth, fresh beginning, gestation, and burial. The surah's dual architecture and exact pre/post-focus repetitions keep several of those readings live at once; the split non-dominant refrain mapping also yields a contained sequel reading that a conservative synthesis would likely lose.
remaining_uncertainties: The context strongly identifies the dual antecedent, but the focus grammar alone does not decide whether the relation is spatial, qualitative, or additive.
Positive descriptions rule out vileness more clearly than they rule out all difference of degree.
Hydraulic, architectural, gestational, and mortuary arrows are reader-supplied mechanisms rather than explicit causal statements.
The non-dominant refrain and close-at-hand outliers should remain resonances, not lexical claims.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **A further pair at a nearer/lower level.** `د و ن/B001` gives nearness short of a limit or a lower position; `ج ن ن` supplies enclosed gardens. The backward dual pronoun establishes comparison with the first pair. I preserve two spatial readings: these gardens may be below the first pair or situated besides/nearer than them. In either case the ayah introduces graded enclosure.
2. **Addition rather than replacement.** The conjunction and second dual repeat the form of 55:46. I infer cumulative layering, not cancellation. The ayah reads as abundance organized into levels.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 55:64's dark saturation, 55:66's gushing springs, and 55:68's named fruits give this pair a distinct material profile. Those later details prevent `دون` from being reduced to simple inferiority.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **`د و ن` `B001` — “nearer, below, or short of a limit,” with `ج ن ن` `B003` — “tree-covered garden.”** Structural cue: `مِن دُونِهِمَا` spatially or hierarchically relates a new dual predicate to a referenced pair. Assigned role: `B001` places this second pair below, nearer than, or on the near side of the prior pair; the token itself does not select among those subscopes. Packet evidence is the prepositional construction and branch range. Inference: the reward domain has relational depth or rank rather than one flat plane. Reading change: the ayah can introduce a tiered garden arrangement.

2. **`د و ن` `B003` — “other than or besides.”** Structural cue: the same construction can mark addition without committing to vertical rank. Assigned role: this branch makes the dual gardens an additional pair. Packet evidence is the accepted alternative and conjunction; inference: recompense expands beyond the referenced pair. Reading change: an additive reading coexists with the spatial/rank reading and is not merged with it.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 55:64–66 confirmed that the newly related pair is internally coherent, but no later ayah in the window resolved `د و ن B001` spatial/rank relation against `B003` addition.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A lower or nearer enclosure becomes so saturated with growth that its green reads as blackness.

concept_gloss.text: bir şeyin ilk ve yeni dönemi

neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal da bir sürecin ilk noktasına veya başlangıç bölümüne yönelir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi sineğin sesinin çoğalmasını açıkça destekler, ancak ikinci biçimin hem uçarken çok ses çıkaran bir böceğe hem de sıklaşan bir bitkiye yorumlanabileceğini söyler; dal yalnızca böcek yorumu altında ses dalıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Ses anlamı böcek yorumu şartına bağlıdır; aynı biçim bitkiyi gösterdiğinde sıklaşma anlamı bu dalın dışında kalır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yalın ses dalı korunur, fakat iki yorumlu biçim yalnızca böcek referansı kesin olduğunda bu tanıma bağlanır.

concept_map.definition: Sineğin veya sinek olarak yorumlanan küçük uçucu canlının uçuş sırasında sesini ve vızıltısını çoğaltmasıdır. Aynı ad bitkiyi gösterirse anlam ses değil, bitkinin sıklaşmasıdır.

facets.statement: Sinek uçarken çıkardığı sesi veya vızıltıyı çoğaltır.
İki yorumlu ad böceği gösterirse uçuş sesi, bitkiyi gösterirse sıklaşıp dolaşma anlamına gelir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar sineğin sesinin çoğalmasını verir; iki yorumlu adın böcek okumasında uçuş vızıltısı, bitki okumasında ise sıklaşma bildirdiğini ayrıca belirtir.

concept_gloss.applicability: Referansın sinek veya benzeri küçük uçucu canlı olduğu ve sesin uçuşta arttığı bağlamlara uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Uçucu böcek katılımcısını, uçuş bağlamını ve sesin çoğalmasını birlikte korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Sinek veya benzeri küçük uçucu canlının çıkardığı sesin çoğalması eylem olarak anlatıldığında doğaldır.

error_profile.preserves: Böcek sesini ve bu sesin miktar veya yoğunluk bakımından artmasını korur.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi göğüs kemiklerini ve kaburgaların göğse yakın uçlarını bildirir; bir kaynak içteki orta kemiği de aynı anatomik bölgeye dahil eder.

full_context_packet.note: surah-scope fallback: the default commentary workflow does not consume per-ayah focus packets, so the source packet is scoped by this builder to roots this ayah can justify and carries no staged reveal order

scoping.note: SCOPED, NOT ABSENT. The surah-scope fallback inventory covers every root in the surah; it is narrowed here to roots this ayah can justify -- roots occurring in this ayah (all their branches kept, unconditionally, because Layer 2 selects nothing) plus roots explicitly cited by channel material anchored here (only the cited branches kept, enough to resolve the citation). A root listed in dropped_roots is a deliberate scoping decision, not a missing source.

v12_reader_responses.note: Per-ayah focus-run reader responses are retired from the default commentary workflow. Use regular reader walks, plus/minus-5 reader walks, and cross-run publication findings for corpus-wide reader-derived evidence.

v12_cross_run_publication.note: Compact final cross-run findings for this ayah, reconciled upstream from regular and plus/minus-5 reader runs; use as a coverage/priority check, not as replacement prose.

butuncul_okuma.note: no whole-surah reading file exists for this surah

occurrence_evidence_trim.note: TRIMMED, NOT ABSENT. dictionary_entry.occurrence_evidence.occurrences and .ayahs are removed from every root by design: they are a per-occurrence QAC concordance and character-span alignment table carrying zero readings, branches or senses, and they dominated bundle size (~1.5 MB for a single common root). occurrence_evidence.summary (corpus frequency) and .forms (inflectional inventory) are retained. Dictionary/gloss branches are kept in full for every included Furuq root target.

branch_policy.note: No branch filtering is applied. Every branch present in each included dictionary/gloss root entry is kept.

root_mapping.policy: Use the dominant Furuq root for every QAC root, and include non-dominant Furuq targets as additional root_lexicon entries when qac-furuq-v4-root-map marks the QAC root as split.

root_lexicon.note: Turkish is the only language with dictionary entries/glosses currently sourced.
